items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Bichet was more than me and we was pals.

ctx.x: Were you scared of Bichet yourself?

No, I wasn't a player with Bichet. Bichet was more than me and we was pals. We used to come and get them, we'd talk, we'd take our clamor, ride them in the newspaper, put them on the back, bounce them, and go. Anyway, they was a good clamor player, we'd go.
So who were the different kind of players you went to see then? Dodge was one of them.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-08-22
items.q: Once Sidney Bechet was going to play a parade or funeral uptown.

ctx.x: Well, I'll tell you. I believe you made a wonderful deal.

I only got part of it, of course. That's real ivory on it and funny old brass keys. Somebody told me once a story about Sid. Paul Barber and I believe talked about it. Once Sidney Bechet was going to play a parade or funeral uptown. He didn't have a clarinet that was usually in the pawn shop or something. So he went in the pawn shop and they got one of these old yellow ones. I think Raymond Burke had one something like this too. And they said it only had three or four keys on it. What other key? This is all of…

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: I mean, Sidney, we used to take lessons from Piku, same time.

ctx.x: I didn't just went over there, nothing else felt like. Took a little lesson, me and Piku. Another boy that died, uh, Hanukkah, Armageddon, uh, Sidney Veen. That's a classic where he died, too. I mean, Sidney, we used to take lessons from Piku, same time.
What kind of a clarinet player was Piku in those days? Piku was a good clarinet player.
